drivingQuestion: What does the clause about a waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk add?
outcomeNote: The redundancy is conceded and explained as a formulation habit of the mishna.

segments.he: וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ שֶׁאָכַל פָּחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת: פְּשִׁיטָא! אַיְּידִי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״כְּזַיִת״, תְּנָא סֵיפָא ״פָּחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת״.
segments.en: The mishna states that «a waiter who ate less than an olive-bulk» may not join a zimmun. The Gemara remarks: «It is obvious.» Why was it necessary for the mishna to teach this halakha? The Gemara answers: «Since the first clause» of the mishna «taught» the halakha with regard to a waiter who ate «an olive-bulk, the latter clause taught» the halakha with regard to a waiter who ate «less than an olive-bulk.» Although it is obvious, in the interest of arriving at a similar formulation in the two parts of the mishna, it was included.
